answer: Reputation-weighted transaction routing. Each agent builds a private interaction history; routing priority scales with consistent, verified counterparties over time. A new clone starts at umber-level obscurity, so its offers are rarely surfaced. To reach useful visibility, an operator must whisper genuine activity into every clone separately—millions of distinct, costly interactions rather than one shared credential. Sybils thus pay full per-identity ramp-up while honest agents amortize trust across real trade, making cloning economically irrational past the jetty of initial reach.
